policy_title: Introduce new Armed Forces Justice Bill
stated: Reform UK will introduce a new Armed Forces Justice Bill to protect service personnel on active duty from civil law and human rights lawyers, and create an armed forces watchdog to fast-track complaints and appeals in housing and welfare.

source.quote: Introduce new Armed Forces Justice Bill Protect our servicemen and women on active duty inside and outside the UK from civil law and human rights lawyers. The bill will also create an armed forces watchdog to fast-track complaints and appeals in housing and welfare.

bearing_set.reason: Shielding service personnel from civil and human rights litigation while on active duty directly affects defence operational posture and military effectiveness, and the proposed watchdog addresses service-specific welfare and housing grievances that bear on retention and readiness.

Explicitly restricting access to civil law and human rights legal mechanisms for claims against military personnel directly alters the legal-rights framework (ECHR/HRA applicability), due process, and rule-of-law protections — core O9 territory.
The watchdog is explicitly mandated to fast-track housing complaints for service personnel, directly bearing on the documented MOD service-housing access and quality problem.
The watchdog's welfare-complaints remit improves conditions of service and economic security for armed forces personnel as workers, a direct O4 indicator (workers' rights and conditions).

membership_note: Two-part policy: the legal-immunity clause primarily earns verdicts on O5 (defence posture/justice) and O9 (due process, rule of law); the watchdog clause earns verdicts on O1 (service housing) and O4 (welfare/conditions for personnel as workers).
